verdict.rationale: Bun's package manager is a standalone CLI that runs on the user's own machine. It keeps a local package cache at a configurable path and documents an offline mode that never touches the network, so the core tool runs on user-controlled infrastructure. It still defaults to the npm registry and advisory endpoint for resolution and audits, and no deployment or source-availability evidence is present. Missing for 10: evidence of open-source or source availability for building and running it yourself, documented support for pointing at a self-hosted or private registry, and independent hands-on corroboration of fully self-hosted operation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: It's a standalone tool that works in existing Node.js projects; if your project has a `package.json`, you can use `bun install`.
Never touch the network (registry, tarball URLs, git); a required dependency that is not cached is an error
Bun stores every package downloaded from the registry in a global cache at `~/.bun/install/cache`, or the path set by the `BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR` environment variable.
